subject: Phased model sunset - alignment, exception ask, and comms
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@acme.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: acme-legal@acme.com
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Phased model sunset - alignment, exception ask, and comms

Jonas / Priyom,

Thanks for the heads up on the upcoming model family changes. Our engineering team reviewed the high-level timeline in the spreadsheet — there are two asks on our side before we can commit to the proposed cutover: 1) an exemption window for our RAG pipeline (we have heavy KV cache reliance), and 2) a written comms draft we can send to our security team to confirm no data-retention changes.

I've attached the Acme-side migration plan (acme_migration_plan.xlsx) showing traffic patterns and peak windows. Goal: minimize retries during our nightly batch jobs. Can Redwood provide a short SLA for throughput during our canary and an explicit fallback model that preserves token semantics?

If it helps, we can do a 30m sync tomorrow morning with product and infra.

— Marta
Senior Platform Engineer, Acme Corp
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@acme.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Phased model sunset - alignment, exception ask, and comms

Marta — thanks, and appreciated the spreadsheet.

Short answers up front: we can offer a 4-week exemption window (can be extended by request) for your RAG pipelines, and we will document the fallback model that preserves token-level semantics (details below). We should absolutely run a canary during your low-traffic window — Priyom, can you confirm resource isolation for the canary and the throughput SLA (tokens/s) we can guarantee?

Proposed next steps:
- Internal: Priyom to validate technical feasibility and fill in the infra SLAs.
- Comms: Stephanie to prepare a joint comms draft using our comm template (redwood_comm_template_v2.docx).
- Product: Marissa / Aditya to approve exception criteria and the official extension process.

I can host the sync tomorrow 09:00 PT. Marta — does that work? If not, propose two slots.

Thanks — Jonas
Strategic Partner Lead, Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das@redwood.com <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, Marta Ruiz <marta@acme.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 13:40:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Phased model sunset - alignment, exception ask, and comms

On Tue, 20 Mar 2028 at 10:03, jonas_weber@redwood.com wrote:
> Proposed next steps:
> - Internal: Priyom to validate technical feasibility and fill in the infra SLAs.

Quick tech note from infra: we can carve a dedicated canary pool for Acme for the duration of the 4-week exemption. That pool will run on a dedicated GPU reservation; throughput guarantee is 900 tokens/s sustained for single-streamed requests at 2k context length. Burst capacity available on request (subject to dedicated-resources cap).

A few asks from our side so we can schedule the pool and avoid noisy neighbors:
- Confirm expected concurrency and typical sequence lengths (approx numbers please).
- Share the exact endpoints + tokenization assumptions used by your RAG pipeline.
- Legal: if Acme cannot accept the SLA, we can document an operational fallback (model_variant_v2) that matches output formats but may differ slightly in latency.

Attaching the comms template we'll use — Stephanie will fill the external language, but I wanted to surface the SLA numbers now so the sync is efficient.

Attachments: redwood_comm_template_v2.docx

— Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, Marta Ruiz <marta@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 16:20:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Phased model sunset - alignment, exception ask, and comms

Thanks team — noting two comm tracks: external technical comms for Acme engineering and a short executive note for Acme security/legal that calls out no changes to retention or telemetry collection.

Draft plan I will prepare before the sync:
- 1-page technical brief (what changes, what stays the same) — to Acme engineering.
- 1-paragraph legal assurance (no change in PII retention; KMS/HSM policies unchanged) — to Acme legal.
- Customer-facing timeline graphic + canary dates.

Jonas: do we have a single source of truth doc (Confluence) that'll be the shared link in the comm? If so I'll link it and include versioning info.

— Stephanie
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, Marta Ruiz <marta@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 14:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Phased model sunset - alignment, exception ask, and comms

Thanks for pulling this together. Approving the 4-week exemption window for Acme with the following guardrails:
- Canary must run in the dedicated pool and be limited to the agreed concurrency. Priyom, confirm schedule and resource reservation by EOD 3/22.
- Stephanie: publish the two comm artifacts and share the Confluence link with version tag v1.1. Use the attached template and mark the legal language as "for review".
- Aditya / Product: document the exception policy and the trigger for extension (customer impact metrics + escrowed rollbacks).
- Jonas: run the joint sync tomorrow at 09:00 PT; include Acme engineering + Acme legal.

I'll stay on the thread as the exec sponsor — if anything moves outside these guardrails, escalate to me directly.

— Marissa Cole
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
